title: In vitro cyst puncture and injury-induced tubule formation using renal epithelial cells
protocol: Trypsinize plMDCK cells that have reached 70%–80% confluence with 1.5 mL Trypsin EDTA.
Pellet trypsinized cells using Heraeus Megafuge 1.0 R at 2,000 rpm and room temperature.
Resolve the cell pellets in 10 mL DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Count the cell number using a Neubauer counting chamber by adding 10 μL of cell suspension to it.
Count all 4 quadrants using a Zeiss Primovert microscope at 10× magnification.
Divide the count by 4 and multiply by 10,000 to obtain the number of cells per mL in the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the amount of medium containing 20,000 cells in a 5 mL reaction tube at 2,000 rpm and room temperature.
Remove the supernatant medium with a pipette while preparing the collagen matrix solution.
Pipette the appropriate amount of PureCol Collagen into a 5 mL reaction tube.
Add the amount of Earle’s Balanced Salt Solution 10× to the mixture.
Add 29 μL of NaOH solution until the color turns pink.
Gently mix the mixture.
Add a few more μL of NaOH using a micro pipette until the solution turns pinkish.
Pipette the collagen mixture onto the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in the collagen mixture.
Pipette 850 μL of the collagen cell suspension per center well dish.
Leave the dishes in the CO2 incubator for 1 hour to allow the collagen to gel.
Add 1 mL of DMEM medium supplemented with forskolin (FSK; 10 mM) on top of each collagen gel.
Change the DMEM medium every 2 days.
Turn on the Keyence microscope including the in vitro chamber 30 minutes prior to injection and puncturing cysts.
Pull glass capillaries using the Four-Step-Micropipette-Puller with settings of 850°C/100% Force/9 Distance.
Grind the pointed side of the pulled capillary using the MicroGrinder at an angle of 30°, water-cooled.
Fill the ground capillary completely with mineral oil from its rear side.
Fill the capillary completely with mineral oil before introducing the injection solution.
Ensure a seamless transition from mineral oil to injection solution without air bubbles.
Extend the pen of the WPI Puller to 88% and secure the capillary on it.
Aspirate the liquid by manually actuating the puller in the solution to be injected, such as brilliant cresyl blue.
Eject the solution a few times to remove any air or oil at the tip of the capillary.
Clamp the pen in the holder.
Place the center well dish with in vitro cysts under the Leica stereomicroscope and lock it into position.
Pierce the cysts in the collagen using the micromanipulator.
Inject 1 nl of volume of brilliant cresyl blue solution (saturated solution) into the punctured cyst.
Pull the capillary quickly out of the cyst after injection to prevent clogging at the tip.
Place the dish with the injected cysts into the live cell imaging chamber of the Keyence microscope.
Search for the colored cysts in the BZ-II Viewer software and record them as viewpoints (x20 magnification).
Image the cysts and the injury-caused induction of tubulogenesis for 72 h (37°C, 5% CO2).
Import live image sequences into ImageJ as a stack.
Set the scale using the corresponding scale bar to obtain the measured distances in μm.
Draw a straight line that matches your scale bar depicted in the image.
Analyze → Set Scale → insert the correct length in the known distance field in “μm” and type “μm” into the field named Unit of length.
If you are going to analyze further stacks with the same resolution, tick global.
Use Plugins → Movies → Timer stamper to insert time according to the frequency used to capture photos.
Fill in the Starting Time: usually 0.00.
Insert Interval (the interval that has been used to capture your photos): in our case 20.00 (min).
Determine the position of your time stamp using X/Y-Location.
Specify the unit used by Suffix: in our case “min”.
Set the starting point of tubule outgrowth and the end point of tubule growth using the multi-point tool.
Mark the point of outgrowth in the first image of your analysis.
Mark the end of the tubule in the last image of your analysis.
Tick show on all slices by double-clicking on the multi-point button.
Go to the last slice, then go to Edit → Draw.
Push “Shift” + “a” to remove your points and find them now fixed in your image.
Draw a straight line between your dots.
Use Analyze → Measure to measure the length between the two dots which will be given in “μm”.
Repeat measurements for all injected cysts.
Transfer data sets to a program that allows statistical analysis.
